Flip: likely resale A$208 (Denhams) less 15% selling commission (A$31) and A$15 outbound postage = A$162 / 2.396 = A$67.6, round down to $65. Pickup Moonah, inbound $0. lots.confidence_reason: Marks read in the photo (duty head, date letter c, lion passant, WS) and weight stated, but only one SOLD entry within 24 months and it is a close rather than exact match; melt value independently supports it.

lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 2 enlarged: four punches plus maker. Profile duty head, lowercase c in a cut-corner cushion (London 1818-19), lion passant, WS in an oval. No separate crowned leopard's head is clearly visible (the first head reads as the sovereign's duty head), which is a minor oddity to check. A stamped or scratched '1819' sits beside the marks. Photo 1 shows script JB initials on every stem front. Photo 3 shows matching marks on all six.
lots.condition: Worn, with light dents and tip wear on bowls (one bowl in photo 1 shows a mark near the tip); engraved initials; marks clear.
lots.question_for_gowans: Do all six carry the leopard's head mark as well as the duty head, date letter c, lion and WS, and are there any splits or repairs to the bowl tips? Is 101.6g the weight of all six?

lots.what_it_is: Set of six sterling silver fiddle pattern teaspoons, London, maker IH, script monogram on the stems, 96.6g total, 13.5cm. Catalogued as John Harris IV, London 1833, but the marks read in the photos (crowned leopard's head, capital S, George III duty head) point to London 1813-14 instead.

lots.working: Keep: Denhams A$208.2 / 1.198 = A$173.8, round down to $170 hammer. Flip: A$208 resale less 15% commission (A$31) and A$15 postage = A$162 / 2.396 = A$67.6, round down to $65. Pickup Moonah, inbound $0. Metal alone about A$249, so $170 hammer (A$204 all-in) sits below melt.

lots.dropped_entries: Denhams lots 194 and 206 (page opened, prices confirmed) dropped: mixed lots of odd Old English spoons, not a matched fiddle set. Silver Spoon Antiques AUD 339 (William Sumner 1830, 190g): page returns 404, snippet only, kept only as a lead. eBay.de GBP 175 London 1831 set: snippet only, eBay closed to us, lead only. Woolley and Wallis lot 60 GBP 572: page came back empty, snippet only, and a George III Hanoverian set with mote spoon, not comparable; dropped.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 3 enlarged (marks run up the stem): IH maker's mark in a rectangle, then a crowned leopard's head in a shaped shield, lion passant, capital roman S in a cut-corner shield, and a sovereign's head with tied hair (George III style). London used a crowned leopard until 1821 and a capital S in 1813-14; 1833 would be a lowercase s, an uncrowned leopard and a William IV head. So the set is probably London 1813-14 and the John Harris IV attribution needs checking. Photo 1 shows a script monogram on each stem; photo 2 shows matching marks on all six.
lots.condition: Mild wear and scratches, bowls look sound, monogrammed; marks crisp.
lots.question_for_gowans: The marks look like London 1813 (crowned leopard, capital S, George III head) rather than 1833; can you confirm the date letter and maker? Any dents or repairs to the bowls, and is 96.6g for all six?
